lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: putting clothes away

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 2 — clothing care and readiness routines
objective: The learner opens their own clothing storage spot, such as a dresser drawer, closet shelf, or a labeled bin, and looks past the top layer to find at least two specific errors from an earlier put-away session, such as a shirt stuffed in sideways, a folded stack that has toppled, or shoes left on the floor instead of their spot, then corrects each one found.
scenario: The learner opens a drawer, shelf, or bin that was filled earlier in the week and checks it item by item instead of only glancing at the top, looking for at least two specific placement errors, then fixes each error one at a time and checks the spot again before closing it.
materials: the learner's own clothing storage spot (drawer, shelf, closet section, or bin)

tasks.directions: Before opening the storage spot, think about how it was left earlier this week.

prompts.text: Guess how many things might be out of place before you open it, and name the spot you are checking.

tasks.directions: Open the storage spot and check it item by item, lifting the top layer to see underneath, instead of dumping everything out.

prompts.text: I opened the spot carefully and checked layer by layer instead of just glancing at the top.
I found error number one and named exactly what was wrong with it.
I found error number two and named exactly what was wrong with it.
I fixed both errors and checked the spot one more time before stopping.

tasks.directions: Check a second storage spot, such as a shoe area or a hook by the door.

prompts.text: Describe one more out-of-place item you found in a second spot and exactly how you fixed it.

tasks.directions: Think back over both errors you found and fixed today.

prompts.text: Describe which of the two errors was easiest to notice and which was hardest to notice, and explain why the hardest one is easy to miss on a quick glance.

remediation: If a learner closes the drawer or door right after a quick glance and reports no errors because 'it looks fine from the top,' reteach by having them physically lift or move the top layer of a known messy spot to reveal what is underneath before making any judgment.
extension: Have the learner apply the same two-error check to a bookshelf or a backpack, looking layer by layer instead of a single glance from the top.
